anomalies.observed: The high-side PMOS Q1 has its gate (pin 1) connected only to jumper JP1 pin 3 and its drain (pin 3) connected to the BASE of the NPN driver Q2 (pin 1). Q2's collector (pin 3) is tied through R2 1K to the PWM net, and Q2's emitter (pin 2) to GND. Thus the MCU PWM signal is not connected to the PMOS gate at all, and the PWM net is instead shorted to ground through Q2's base-emitter junction whenever the fan supply (VCC_OUT) is present.
anomalies.expected: In a PWM-controlled high-side fan driver the NPN's collector must drive the PMOS gate (pulling it low to turn the switch on) and its base must be driven from the MCU PWM line through a series resistor. The spec describes an 'ATtiny-driven fan controller', i.e. the MCU PWM output is intended to regulate the fan.

evidence.quote: Page 1, sheet /: Q1 (Q_PMC_GSD) pin 1 → JP1 pin 3; Q1 pin 3 → Q2 (BC817) pin 1; Q2 pin 3 → R2 1K → PWM label; Q2 pin 2 → GND

anomalies.impact: The MCU cannot PWM-control the high-side switch; with the fan supply energised Q2 forward-biases and clamps the PWM net to ~0.7 V, so the fan's own PWM input is held low and the fan runs at full speed regardless of the controller output. The board does not behave as a speed-controllable fan controller.

parsed.summary: The fan-driver stage is mis-wired: the PMOS gate is not driven by the NPN transistor (the NPN collector sits on the PWM net and its base on the fan-supply node), so the MCU PWM output is shorted to ground through Q2 and the fan cannot be speed-controlled as the 'ATtiny-driven fan controller' intends.
